explanation: Pterosaurs, pterodactyls included, were flying reptiles: close cousins of the dinosaurs, but on a separate branch. The dinosaurs that really took to the air became birds.

claims.text: Pterodactyls and other pterosaurs were not dinosaurs.
Pterosaurs were flying reptiles closely related to dinosaurs but on a separate branch of the reptile family tree.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Pterosaurs are not dinosaurs. Under the standard definition, dinosaurs are the descendants of the last common ancestor of Saurischia and Ornithischia, and that group excludes pterosaurs. Pterosaurs are often referred to by popular media or the general public as "flying dinosaurs", but they remain outside the dinosaur group.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Most paleontologists place birds within Theropoda as a specialized subgroup, specifically within Maniraptora (index 3-9). Because of this, birds are the only surviving dinosaurs (index 3-1).
